title: KeyBroker Terraform module: multi-KMS/HSM mediation, secrets failover, and staged upgrade playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (KeyBroker) that standardizes wiring between our Private control plane and customer KMS/HSM providers, enables dual-write key provisioning, and exposes automated health and canary upgrade checks. This module will be used in VPC/private deployments to ensure seamless upgrades from cloud KMS to HSM-backed key providers (and back) without secrets outage. It must support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and an on-prem HSM gateway (Thales/Entrust) via a pluggable provider interface. The module also includes optional integrations for Secrets Manager and HashiCorp Vault for credential/secret material syncing and optional envelope encryption patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module creates provider-agnostic key bindings and outputs a stable key identifier that the control plane can consume
Module supports dual-write mode: keys/material can be mirrored to a secondary provider and verified via test vectors
Healthcheck resources and scripts run in Terraform plan/apply that validate sign/verify for each provider endpoint
Upgrade playbook (documented) demonstrates staged canary rollout from cloud-KMS -> HSM with automated smoke tests and rollback hooks
Integration tests (HCL + wrapper scripts) run in CI for AWS/GCP/Azure + a simulated HSM gateway image
Security review notes included: FIPS path validation, import vs. generated keys policy, and HSM attestation handling
tasks: Draft module interface and variables (provider blocks, key_policy, lifecycle options)
Implement provider adapters for aws, google, azurerm, and an hsm_provider shim
Add null_resource-based health probes that run sign/verify and return metric tags
Create test harness (dockerized HSM emulator + local Vault) for CI
Document staged upgrade and rollback steps with clear pre-checks
Add example usage for private deployment template and dedicated capacity stacks
Security review and threat model session with Security team
Open initial PR and iterate on review feedback
